variables.name: Air temperature near the surface
variables.definition: How warm the air is about 2 m above the ground, like a weather-station thermometer.
variables.why_it_trends: Greenhouse-gas warming raises it almost everywhere, faster over land and the Arctic.

variables.name: Precipitation (corrected)
variables.definition: The amount of rain and snow that falls, as water depth per day.
variables.why_it_trends: Warming changes storm tracks and moisture, so some regions get wetter and others drier.

variables.name: Root-zone soil wetness
variables.definition: How full the soil near plant roots is with water, shown in percent of saturation (0% = bone dry, 100% = soaked).
variables.why_it_trends: Shifts in rainfall and higher evaporation from warming can dry or wet soils over decades.

variables.name: Sunlight reaching the ground
variables.definition: Energy from the Sun arriving at the surface per day, after clouds and haze.
variables.why_it_trends: Cleaner air ("brightening") or more clouds/aerosols ("dimming") change it.

variables.name: Snow depth
variables.definition: How deep the snow layer on the ground is.
variables.why_it_trends: Warmer winters shorten the snow season and reduce snowpack in many mid-latitude regions.

variables.name: Air temperature at 2 m (MERRA-2 grid)
variables.definition: Near-surface air temperature from NASA's MERRA-2 reanalysis, which blends observations into a weather model.
variables.why_it_trends: See air temperature; gridded field enables trend maps.

variables.name: Haze / aerosol optical depth
variables.definition: How much tiny airborne particles (dust, smoke, pollution) dim sunlight passing through the atmosphere.
variables.why_it_trends: Air-quality laws reduce it in some regions while industrial growth or wildfires raise it elsewhere.

variables.name: Precipitation (GPM IMERG satellite)
variables.definition: Rain and snowfall estimated from a constellation of satellites led by NASA's GPM mission.
variables.why_it_trends: Same as precipitation; satellite view covers oceans and remote land.

variables.name: Nitrogen dioxide pollution (OMI)
variables.definition: The amount of NO2 gas, mostly from cars, power plants and industry, in the lower atmosphere above an area.
variables.why_it_trends: Emission controls lower it in many US/European/Chinese cities while growth raises it elsewhere — a classic opposite-trend example.

variables.name: Total ozone column (OMI)
variables.definition: All the ozone in a column of air above a point, in Dobson units; most of it is in the stratospheric ozone layer.
variables.why_it_trends: Recovery after the Montreal Protocol vs. climate-driven circulation changes.

variables.name: Surface air temperature (AIRS satellite)
variables.definition: Near-surface air temperature measured from space by the AIRS infrared sounder.
variables.why_it_trends: Independent satellite cross-check of reanalysis warming.

variables.name: Total water vapour (AIRS)
variables.definition: All the water vapour in a column of air, as if condensed into a layer of water.
variables.why_it_trends: Warmer air holds about 7% more moisture per °C.

variables.name: Topsoil moisture (GLDAS)
variables.definition: Water stored in the top 10 cm of soil, from NASA's land-surface model driven by observations.
variables.why_it_trends: Drought-prone regions can dry as evaporation outpaces rainfall.

variables.name: Evapotranspiration (GLDAS)
variables.definition: Water leaving the land into the air through evaporation and plant "breathing" (transpiration).
variables.why_it_trends: Warming and greening increase it where water is available.

variables.name: Surface runoff (GLDAS)
variables.definition: Rain or snowmelt water that flows over the ground into streams instead of soaking in — a proxy for streamflow.
variables.why_it_trends: Changes in heavy rain, snowmelt timing and land use.

variables.name: Snow water equivalent (GLDAS)
variables.definition: How much water the snowpack would make if melted.
variables.why_it_trends: Warming reduces snowpack and shifts melt earlier.

variables.name: Total water storage (GRACE/GRACE-FO)
variables.definition: All water on and under the land — snow, soil, lakes and groundwater — measured from tiny changes in Earth's gravity.
variables.why_it_trends: Groundwater pumping and ice loss lower it in some regions while others gain water — strong opposite-sign trends.

variables.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI, MODIS)
variables.definition: A satellite index of how green and leafy plants are, from -1 to 1; dense forest is near 0.8.
variables.why_it_trends: Longer growing seasons and CO2 fertilisation "green" some regions; drought and deforestation "brown" others.

variables.name: Land surface temperature (MODIS, daytime)
variables.definition: How hot the ground itself is (not the air), seen by satellite during the day.
variables.why_it_trends: Urban growth (heat islands), deforestation and drying soils heat the surface.

variables.name: Snow cover (MODIS)
variables.definition: The percentage of the ground covered by snow in a month.
variables.why_it_trends: Warming shortens the snow season, especially in spring.

variables.name: Sea surface temperature (MODIS Aqua)
variables.definition: Temperature of the top layer of the ocean seen from space.
variables.why_it_trends: Oceans absorb most of the extra heat from global warming; currents create regional differences.
